skills.name: Practical work 1: death rate and natural increase

note.text:
The crude death rate (DR) is the number of deaths in a year for every 1000 people: DR = (deaths ÷ population) × 1000, in ‰.
The rate of natural increase (NI) is the birth rate minus the death rate: NI = BR − DR, in ‰. Divide by 10 to give it as a percentage: 25 ‰ = 2.5 %.
Natural increase in numbers = births − deaths (migration is not counted).
If BR is greater than DR the population grows; if they are equal it stays the same; if DR is greater it falls (natural decrease).
Example: BR = 38 ‰, DR = 12 ‰, so NI = 26 ‰ = 2.6 % a year.

worked_example.problem: A country has a birth rate of {br} ‰ and a death rate of {dr} ‰. Find its rate of natural increase in ‰ and in %.
steps: As a percentage: {br - dr} ÷ {ten} = {(br - dr) / ten} %.

cards.idea: The death rate is deaths per thousand people in a year.
Natural increase = birth rate − death rate.
Divide a rate in ‰ by ten to give it as a percentage.

check.prompt: A country's rate of natural increase is {n} ‰. What is it as a percentage?

misconceptions.explain: Divide by {ten}: a percentage is per hundred.

questions.prompt: A town of {p} people had {d} deaths in a year. What is its death rate (in ‰)?

misconceptions.explain: Multiply by {k} to get deaths per thousand.

questions.prompt: A country has BR = {br} ‰ and DR = {dr} ‰. What is its rate of natural increase (in ‰)?

misconceptions.explain: Natural increase is births minus deaths: subtract.
Subtract the death rate from the birth rate.

misconceptions.explain: Divide by {ten}: a percentage is per hundred.
